notes: slices: std slice, Vec and Iterator methods. Go's BinarySearch is the leftmost position (partition_point), CompactFunc compares with the original predecessor (rust_stdlib::collections::compact_by), and float ordering and Min/Max follow Go's NaN rules through rust_stdlib::math::{compare, minimum, maximum}. SortFunc and SortedFunc are rust_stdlib::collections::sort_unstable_by, Go's own algorithm, so equal elements are ordered as in Go; the stable sorts are std's, whose order is unique; MaxFunc needs .rev() to return Go's first maximum and CompareFunc/EqualFunc are zip expressions (see each note).

BinarySearch.note: leftmost position; found is a comparison at that index

BinarySearchFunc.note: leftmost position; found is a comparison at that index

Clip.note: shrink_to_fit removes unused capacity; the allocator may keep more than len, where Go's Clip sets cap exactly to len.

CompactFunc.note: compares each element with its original predecessor; Vec::dedup_by compares with the last kept element

CompareFunc.note: Iterator::cmp takes no comparison function: a.iter().zip(b).map(|(x, y)| cmp(x, y)).find(|o| o.is_ne()).unwrap_or_else(|| a.len().cmp(&b.len())), which is Go's order (checked by tests/std_mapping_ties.rs); the result is an Ordering where Go returns the cmp value.

DeleteFunc.note: retain the negation; the predicate runs once per element in order

EqualFunc.note: Iterator::eq takes no equality function: a.len() == b.len() && a.iter().zip(b).all(|(x, y)| eq(x, y)).

Grow.note: Vec::reserve grows to at least the requested capacity, but the resulting cap() follows std's allocator growth, not Go's growslice size classes (reflect ports those for its own values).

IsSorted.note: floats: is_sorted_by(|a, b| math::compare(a, b).is_le()), because slice::is_sorted rejects NaN where Go sorts NaN first

IsSortedFunc.note: Go reports false when cmp(s[i], s[i-1]) < 0: is_sorted_by(|a, b| cmp(b, a).is_ge())

Max.note: floats: fold with rust_stdlib::math::maximum (NaN propagates, +0 above -0)

MaxFunc.note: Iterator::max_by returns the last maximal element and Go the first, so iterate in reverse: s.iter().rev().max_by(|a, b| cmp(a, b)).

Min.note: floats: fold with rust_stdlib::math::minimum (NaN propagates, -0 below +0)

MinFunc.note: Iterator::min_by returns the first minimal element, as Go does: s.iter().min_by(|a, b| cmp(a, b)); do not reverse it.

Sort.note: Exact for integers and strings, whose equal elements are indistinguishable; floats (NaN first, -0 equal to +0) go through rust_stdlib::collections::sort_unstable_by with math::compare so equal elements end up where Go puts them.

SortFunc.note: Go's pdqsort ported, so elements that compare equal come out in Go's order (slice::sort_unstable_by orders them differently); checked against Go in tests/collections_sort.rs.

SortStableFunc.note: The stable order is unique, so sort_by matches Go.

SortedStableFunc.note: collect, then sort_by; the stable order is unique, so it matches Go.
